title: One plus one equals two
summary: In the declared Peano rewrite kernel, the closed term adding one to one normalizes to two.

context.note: Revision 2 binds its exact statement and structured derivation to a deterministic certificate and pinned dependencies.

assumptions.text: The two recursive addition equations are used as oriented rewrite rules.
The symbols 0 and S belong to the declared natural-number presentation.

content.plain: The kernel expands addition once, then removes addition by zero, leaving exactly the term used to define two.
content.exact: With 1:=S(0), 2:=S(S(0)), add(a,0)→a, and add(a,S(b))→S(add(a,b)), the closed term add(1,1) normalizes by two certified rewrites to 2.
content.caveat: This establishes syntactic normalization in the declared rewrite kernel. It does not by itself prove soundness of a broader arithmetic theory.

verification.method: Structured rewrite replay bound to the exact subject, exact statement, dependency digests, kernel rules, and checker bytes.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Supersedes the demonstration whose certificate was not cryptographically or semantically bound to its subject. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
